body:
Three readings are now on the table and none can be eliminated from the text alone. The account reads the trouble as underspecified agreements; the objection adds renegotiation and legitimacy readings and pushes the form of the conversations forward; the rival adds the question of what kind of household this even is. All three flagged their own uncertainty, and a fourth cycle would most likely produce a fourth reading. So the useful move now is to prune rather than to add: say what survives, what is robust across every reading, and which observations do the sorting.

Two corrections to the record first. The objection under-weights the account's own machinery: the third column, what happens when someone cannot do the task, is already a renegotiation protocol. It does not touch legitimacy, but 'say so the day before and the other two decide' is precisely a rule for what happens when terms stop binding. And the objection's sequencing criticism is right but must be applied symmetrically. If thin material does not license ordering, that condemns the rival's ontology-first sequence and the objection's form-first ordering as much as the account's chores-first one. Every ordering does prescriptive work the evidence cannot carry. The defensible rule when evidence cannot rank hypotheses is different: order moves by cost, reversibility, and information yield under all of them. That dissolves most of the sequencing dispute.

Applied, that rule yields a first move neither the account nor the rival proposed. The shared spec note, which on the rival's own argument enacts one reading, and the ontological question, which is a heavy conversation to hand someone already withdrawing, both hand the avoiding flatmate a frame. The rival's opening is contraindicated by the very datum it is meant to explain. The lowest-stakes opening is the account's one-to-one approach with the content stripped of frames: not 'can we sort the bins', not 'what do you take this flat to be', but an unframed question about what makes these conversations bad, kept short, with refusal accepted as an answer. The rival's insistence that separate conversations stay separate applies.

The convergent remedy, though, is the rival's step three, and it should move from afterthought to centerpiece, with one caveat. Owned zones, or a rotation with automatic defaults and a named fallback, is the most reading-robust instrument anyone has proposed. Under ambiguity it is a specification; under renegotiation it supplies the fallback; under legitimacy it de-personalizes enforcement, since the schedule does the nagging rather than a flatmate; under the conversational-form reading it reduces the number of negotiations; under the privacy reading, unaudited zones are close to what that flatmate would want. Here the rival's neutrality point is half right and its implied contrast is wrong: not specifying also enacts a reading, the reading that nothing is discussable. Neutrality is unavailable anywhere; the substitute is reversibility. Propose the default as explicitly provisional, revisable at a scheduled check-in.

The one reading nothing above addresses is distribution. The objection's imbalance point and the rival's own caution both survive here: tighter specs on a lopsided arrangement are a lopsided arrangement with clearer paperwork, and fixed zones can entrench lopsidedness if the zones differ in burden. The fix is to make fairness a design parameter, rotating or swapping zones on a schedule, so distribution is argued about as arrangement rather than as character. The account's advice to avoid moral language cannot be absolute: at some point the split has to be sayable, just not as a grievance about a person.

What I would downgrade rather than discard: the tests. A fall in recurrence is weaker confirmation than the account implied, but the objection, by naming what the rivals forecast, displacement to fresh complaint items and resurgence at the next schedule change, strengthened the test it attacked. A fall that holds through one schedule change with no new items appearing is real support for the ambiguity reading; displacement or resurgence points at load or legitimacy. The rival's proposed discriminator is weaker than claimed: pulling back from the form of a proposal is also the predicted behavior under the conversational-form reading, since a written proposal from the two engaged flatmates can reproduce exactly the group dynamic the avoider is escaping. More generally, every test routed through the withdrawn flatmate is confounded by the withdrawal itself; their behavior is the least interpretable part of the system precisely because their reasons are the least accessible. So route the discriminating observation through the arguments that still happen: 'that is not what we said', 'my shift changed', and 'why is it always you raising it' are three different problems wearing the same chore, and the exact wording of the next few disputes will do most of the sorting for free.

What I leave open: which reading is true; why the friend withdrew, the single datum most likely to prune the field and obtainable only by the asker; and where the third flatmate actually stands, since nothing in the material says the asker has an ally. Further analysis without those has diminishing returns. Compressed: do not choose a diagnosis first. Make the moves that are safe under every reading, one unframed conversation, a provisional default with scheduled revisability, fairness handled as design, and let the household's own behavior decide what the problem was. If, after two genuine low-pressure attempts, a flatmate declines any arrangement whatever its shape, the question stops being about chores, and naming the living-arrangement question then rather than deferring it is the one thing all three contributions agree on.

consistent with c6."},{"id":"k1","type":"commitment","text":"Open with an unframed one-to-one invitation to the avoiding flatmate: ask what is making these conversations bad, propose nothing, keep it short, and accept refusal as an answer.","scope":"The next one or two weeks; one conversation.","action":"A 10-15 minute private conversation with no agenda and no frame, keeping separate conversations separate per rival#r10.","consequence":"Either obtains the datum most likely to prune the readings, or the refusal itself is informative.","revises":["account#c3"],"depends":["c1"]},{"id":"k2","type":"commitment","text":"Propose a provisional default arrangement, owned zones or an automatic rotation with a named fallback, framed as reducing the number of things requiring discussion and explicitly revisable at a scheduled check-in with amendments invited.","action":"Frame it as fewer things to argue about, not as a fairness settlement; set a revisability checkpoint.","consequence":"Safe under all readings and reversible if experienced as side-taking; addresses ambiguity, renegotiation, legitimacy and form at once.","depends":["c4","c3"]},{"id":"k3","type":"commitment","text":"Make distribution a design parameter: rotate or swap zones on a schedule so fairness is argued about as arrangement rather than as character, and do not interpret refusal to discuss character as refusal to rebalance load.","consequence":"Addresses the one reading k2 does not, without converting it into a grievance conversation.","depends":["c5"]},{"id":"k4","type":"commitment","text":"Record the exact wording of the next two or three disputes without intervening, and sort them into what did we agree, does it still bind, and who has standing to raise it, before drawing any conclusion.","consequence":"Turns ordinary arguments into discriminating observations at almost no cost.","depends":["c6"]},{"id":"k5","type":"commitment","text":"Keep the convergent escalation trigger: if after two genuine low-pressure attempts a flatmate declines any arrangement whatever its shape, name the living-arrangement question explicitly rather than deferring it.","consequence":"Prevents both indefinite deferral and forcing a large decision from a chore dispute; the one point all three contributions converge on.","revises":["rival#r11"]},{"id":"p1","type":"problem","text":"Why the friend withdrew remains unknown and is the single datum most likely to prune the readings; the asker may find the disagreement runs in more than one direction and should not assume an ally."},{"id":"u1","type":"use","text":"Take up the rival's instruction to keep separate conversations separate, the account's insistence on small concrete scope, and the objection's demand that rival readings stand side by side, as the operating method for the next stage.","depends":["c1"],"mentions":["rival#r10","objection#u1"]}],"uptake":["c1","c3","c4","c5","c6","o1","o2","o3","o4","k1","k2","k3","k4","k5","p1","p2","u1"]}
